{#y9ys} # Discussion

{#poer} Our study investigated the outcomes of lung cancer surgery in elderly patients, focusing on postoperative complications and mortality rates. We observed an in-hospital mortality rate of 1.7% after lung cancer surgery. Benker et al. [@w:w6] reported an overall operative mortality rate of 1.56%, similar to our finding. In contrast, Detillon et al. [@w:w7] found a higher operative mortality rate by 2.1% in patients ≥ 60 years with lung cancer resections compared to our data.

{#mal5} ## Postoperative complications

{#yokc} We found that 28.9% of patients experienced postoperative pulmonary complications and 12.6% experienced cardiac complications classified as Clavien–Dindo grade ≥ II. These rates are higher compared to the previous studies reporting 10–15.4% for pulmonary complications in elderly patients undergoing lung resection [@w:w8]. Similary, Calado et al. [@w:w9] reported lower cardiac complications rates (8.2%) compared to our findings. In contrast, Srisomboon et al. [@w:w10] reported higher rate of respiratory (25%) and lower rates of cardiac complications (6%) in elderly patients undergoing thoracoscopic surgery.

{#tj9u} # Predictors associated with Clavien–Dindo complications in lung cancer surgery: A retrospective cohort study

{#hjb9} # Abstract

{#nzop} **Background: **To highlight the risk assessment tool associated with postoperative cardiopulmonary complications of Clavien–Dindo (CD) ≥ II in elderly patients who underwent lung cancer surgery.

{#b223} **Methods: **In patients ≥ 60 years admitted during 2020–2023 and having undergone lung cancer surgery, postoperative cardiopulmonary complications were examined using the CD classification as groups (CD grade I versus ≥ II), and the risk factors were analyzed using logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves.

{#na19} **Results: **Of the 239 elderly patients, 29.3% had postoperative complications (CD ≥ II). {#vxfu} # Introduction

{#rlne} Lung cancer is the most frequently occurring cancer and the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide . Pulmonary resection is key treatment for lung cancer but is often accompanied by significant postoperative complications, which may prolong hospital stay and incur greater medical expenses [@w:w1]. Surgical approaches for lung cancer, including video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and thoracotomy, offer distinct advantages and challenges. Previous studies [@w:w2] suggest that VATS is superior to thoracotomy due to fewer postoperative complications.

{#b9y5} Patients undergoing thoracic surgery were more likely to be older. Poor physiological changes are common in elderly patients with complex comorbidities, which could complicate major noncardiac surgery, especially thoracic surgery, and negatively impact outcomes [@w:w3]. The risk of cardiopulmonary complications increases with age [@w:w4] and the incidence, characteristics, and risk factors of postoperative cardiopulmonary complications in noncardiac surgery in elderly patients could be different from those in the general population. It is imperative to evaluate better risk indicators to improve preoperative cardiac risk prediction in elderly patients.
